Actually, I think I see the problem now. When the shell restricts visibility to physical GPU 1, that GPU appears as logical device 0 within the process. If the Python script then sets `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1` again, it's trying to select the second visible GPU—but there's only one visible GPU, so this would actually hide all GPUs and force the model onto CPU. That would explain the low memory usage. `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` refers to physical GPU indices, not logical ones—so when the parent process sets it to `1`, the CUDA driver sees physical GPU 1, and when the child process also sets it to `1` via `os.environ`, it's seeing the same physical GPU. The tmux wrapper doesn't change this behavior since it's just a shell process inheriting the environment.

The low memory usage might indicate the models are still initializing, or the training output I saw earlier could've been from a previous run that wasn't properly cleaned up before resubmitting.
